additional_info.subject: RE: 0403126 - ID0403126-DC/Si-D/IR- [MP / S2 170003301] BRITE- Multiple sessions not starting on connector 1 CRM:02023000464
additional_info.body:
Hi Des,
I’m not getting all the comms between the support team and Colin, so I am not 100% sure what has passed through that channel – but the situation is:
The charger firmware was corrupted, so to bring it back online we had to do a fresh firmware install which gives the charger a new Identity in our system
That new Identity was linked with a temporary serial number, as you can’t have two instances of the same serial number in the database
The intention was to clear from the database the “old” instance of the charger, then revert the new instance to the correct serial number
This is a function that only our senior Level 3 support can do (I don’t have sufficient admin privileges to do it) – that support was booked for today, and should be done by the end of today
In the meantime, Colin raised a new ticket using the (correct) physical serial number for the charger, and the support team told him that charger was offline – which from their point of view is correct as they were looking at the old deprecated instance of the charger ID.
Bringing a charger online with a temporary serial number is a very unusual thing to do, so there’s no procedure for this to be communicated to the Level 2 support team – we had expected to clean and correct the database before they would need to deal with the temporary change.
We told L2 support the serial number had changed, which resulted in a reply to Colin that we had the “wrong” serial number – this is true, but only half the story (as above).
I will ensure that the temporary serial number is corrected today, so any future tickets will not result in such confusion.
Thanks,
Jason

additional_info.subject: RE: 0403126 - ID0403126-DC/Si-D/IR- [MP / S2 170003301] BRITE- Multiple sessions not starting on connector 1 CRM:02023000464
additional_info.body:
We have investigated the reported issues between the 21st January and the 1st February and we have not found any systematic charger problems which would inhibit charging - we see a lot of instances of the charger timing out waiting for authorisation to start from the back office. This would affect both App and Contactless transactions, since both are dependent on the Fuuse backoffice to send remote starts.
Since 1st February 13:39 the charger has been set to "inoperative" from the Fuuse back office over OCPP. This puts all outlets in an out-of-order state. This was not done by Siemens.
During the investigations, we have found that the connection to OCPP is frequently lost, with evidence of a poor signal strength and low bandwidth at the charger. This is likely to be a contributory factor in the issues prior to the 1st February.

additional_info.subject: Re: 0403126 - ID0403126-DC/Si-D/IR- [MP / S2 170003301] BRITE- Multiple sessions not starting on connector 1 CRM:02023000464

Jason, you have not addressed the ongoing issue of charge sessions being aborted. Orange screen Error "Charging Aborted".
Premature endings / session failures were reported throughout January and last week also. Regarding sessions not starting, Fuuse are either not receiving the command from you to start the charge or you are not sending the command to them, this is an OCPP communication error.
On the flip side, how, if Fuuse has started a session and the session is going fine, do you explain "charging aborted" sessions, the last session before we had to close on Saturday showed this exact error. How can this be Fuuse's fault?
Where is our on site support today? The site is still closed and we have heard nothing.

additional_info.subject: RE: 0403126 - ID0403126-DC/Si-D/IR- [MP / S2 170003301] BRITE- Multiple sessions not starting on connector 1 CRM:02023000464
additional_info.body:
The specific case mentioned below – logs show the charge was aborted by the car at 13:22. During the charging session, the car changed the Pilot State to B, which is not a valid condition during a charge session, and as a result the charger ramped down and closed the session. There is no fault evident on the charger at or before this time.
Regarding “Fuuse not receiving the command” – the charger doesn’t send the command to start a charge. Fuuse sends us the command (Remote Start) in response to Fuuse receiving authorisation from your Payter terminal or from their own internal app authorisation. In response to a user plugging in, we DO send a request to Fuuse for authentication, and that is clearly evident in our logs. We see a high proportion of incidences where that authentication request times out without a response from Fuuse.
I maintain that with all the evidence we have, there is no problem with the charger. The majority of the problems come down to timeouts communicating with Fuuse. As we have said before, the mobile bandwidth at that site is often very low – signal strength is usually good, but 4G bandwidth is not. We can clearly see this in the amount of timeouts with communications to Fuuse, and the amount that we lose connection to Fuuse completely.

Regarding “Fuuse not receiving the command” – the charger doesn’t send the command to start a charge. Fuuse sends us the command (Remote Start) in response to Fuuse receiving authorisation from your Payter terminal or from their own internal app authorisation. In response to a user plugging in, we DO send a request to Fuuse for authentication, and that is clearly evident in our logs. We see a high proportion of incidences where that authentication request times out without a response from Fuuse.
I maintain that with all the evidence we have, there is no problem with the charger. The majority of the problems come down to timeouts communicating with Fuuse. As we have said before, the mobile bandwidth at that site is often very low – signal strength is usually good, but 4G bandwidth is not. We can clearly see this in the amount of timeouts with communications to Fuuse, and the amount that we lose connection to Fuuse completely.
